open_points.subject: store failure while recording cleanup_failed
open_points.text: If the store refused that record
open_points.question: Does “refused” mean every failed store call that would record the cleanup failure, or only a particular store result, and which exact store result triggers the retry rule?
options: Only an explicitly classified store refusal
Only a failure proven to have written no record
open_points.default_guess: Treat every failed store call for that record as the condition, relying on A18 to guarantee that no record changed.

open_points.subject: admission after an unrecorded cleanup failure
open_points.text: and the next start executes the element again (K-09, A03 rule 7).
open_points.question: For an admission execution whose cleanup-failure TrialExecution could not be stored, does startup retry anything automatically, or does admission wait for another implementation submission as A04 rule 2 specifies?
options: Startup automatically retries the failed trial-case execution
Startup automatically reruns the whole admission
Startup does nothing; a later submission reruns admission afresh
The retry rule applies only to function elements of runs
open_points.default_guess: Limit automatic startup retry to function elements of runs; admission waits for another submission and then reruns the whole corpus.

witness.initial: An implementation is being admitted over cases c1 and c2; c1 has a recorded passing TrialExecution, c2 finishes with unconfirmed cleanup, and the store call for c2's cleanup_failed TrialExecution fails.
events: An authoring agent submits the implementation.
The kernel records c1, executes c2, cannot confirm cleanup, fails to store c2's record, answers internal_error and stops.
The owner restarts the kernel without submitting the implementation again.
outcomes: The new State 5 sentence causes startup to execute c2 again, or to resume admission automatically.
A04 rule 2 leaves admission without a verdict and runs it afresh only after a later submission.
witness.observer: The submitting agent sees either new TrialExecution or verdict/activation records immediately after restart, or no such records until another submission.

open_points.subject: recovery granularity for an interrupted admission
open_points.text: the next start executes the element again
open_points.question: If this sentence applies to admission, what durable work item is “the element”: only the trial case whose record failed, every case in that admission, or a newly started admission over the then-current corpus, and how is the pending admission identified?
options: Retry only the failed trial case and continue using earlier TrialExecutions
Rerun the original admission corpus from its first case
Rerun admission over the corpus current at restart
Record a pending-admission work item before execution so startup can identify it
open_points.default_guess: Do not recover admission automatically; require a new submission, which reruns admission over the current corpus as A04 specifies.

witness.initial: A corpus contains c1 and c2, and no AdmissionVerdict exists for the submitted implementation.
events: Admission records a passing execution for c1.
Execution of c2 has unconfirmed cleanup and its TrialExecution cannot be stored.
Before restart, another permitted request cannot occur because the process stops; after restart the corpus may later grow before resubmission.
outcomes: A recovery implementation reuses c1 and retries only c2.
Another implementation treats admission as incomplete and reruns every case, producing another execution for c1.
witness.observer: The agent inspecting trial evidence sees different TrialExecution counts and possibly a verdict covering a different corpus.

open_points.subject: explicit try after an unrecorded cleanup failure
open_points.text: and the next start executes the element again (K-09, A03 rule 7).
open_points.question: Does startup retry an explicit try operation, and if so where are its selected case list and requesting actor recovered from and what is written to TrialExecution.executed_by?
options: Do not retry; the agent must issue another try request
Persist enough intent to retry the same selected cases and retain the original agent as executed_by
Retry the same cases as startup recovery performed by the kernel
Retry all cases rather than the request's selected subset
open_points.default_guess: Do not retry an explicit try automatically; return internal_error, stop, and require a new agent request.

witness.initial: An agent explicitly tries an implementation on only case c2 of a corpus containing c1 and c2.
events: The c2 sandbox execution ends with unconfirmed cleanup.
The store call for its TrialExecution fails, so neither the selected-case request nor the execution record is durable.
The kernel answers internal_error, stops, and is restarted.
outcomes: Reading the new sentence broadly, startup repeats c2 and records a TrialExecution, with an implementer choosing either the original agent or kernel as executed_by.
Reading startup recovery as A14 defines it, no try occurs; the agent must send another request.
witness.observer: The agent sees either an unsolicited TrialExecution after restart or no execution, and may see a different executed_by actor.
